visual_brief: Khan Tengri is a steep marble pyramid capped with snow and ice above the Inylchek glaciers. Classic views show its snowy southern pyramid or its darker, ribbed north face, which turns gold at sunset. Distinguish it from the nearer Chapaev peak and the much broader Pobeda massif; northern viewpoints can make Chapaev appear taller.
notes: Six distinct JPEGs visually checked; all long sides >=1600 px, five >=2400 px. c1 and c2 are strongest. Flickr originals were inaccessible; small, obscured and unsuitable alternatives were discarded. Licence is unknown where the source states no reuse licence; c6 reproduces the source-page rights wording.
